title: He Blew Up an Entire Inn With One Spell . . . Then Played the Victim (Part 5)
caption:
In The Swordmaster's Youngest Son, Jin Runcandel is sent to the lawless region of Mahmeet to kill a count's son.
He blows up the whole inn with a lightning spell, then plays the frightened survivor. Part 5 ends with the hunter helping him up.

Follow for Part 6!

credit: Swordmaster's Youngest Son (Hwangze Penguin / Mr. Big / AZI)
comment: Was Jin right to blow up the whole inn for one target, or did he go too far? Why?

segments.say: Jin blows up a whole inn with a spell nobody his age should have, then plays the *scared* survivor.
To see how it got here, go back to the end of part four, where Elder Jed is about to *kill* Jin.
Jin stays calm. He says he only attacks people he can *beat*, and he can't beat Jed. Yet.
Jed grins, then bursts out *laughing* in front of the whole class.
Then he says fine, your claim is *acknowledged*. Main-character energy, honestly.
That night Jin goes home, where Gilly waits and Murakhan, a dragon pretending to be a *cat*, sits on his sword.
Jin tells her he cut down a cadet who stood beside the Tona twins. Gilly looks *horrified*.
Turns out that cadet belonged to his sisters' *faction*. Oops.
The rule is simple. Flagbearers only fight other flagbearers, so his sisters can't touch him *directly*.
So they'll mess with his *missions* instead, and Jin loves that. Nobody watches a solo mission, so he can use all his power.
He tells Murakhan he's not taking him along, and the cat gets lifted like a *laundry* bag.
Next morning Elder Jed shows the cadets the family *secret* training.
The Runcandel style has no set moves. It's just a blessed bloodline and a body built to *crush*.
The tool is a singing *stone*. Hit it softly and it thuds, hit it perfectly and it chimes.
Hit it too hard and it *explodes*. Jed shows them, and the yard goes up in smoke.
Jin sees it coming and screams get down, shoving the twins out of the *way*.
Jed says only Luna ever walked away from this clean, until *now*. Jin dodged the whole thing.
His reward is brutal. Every afternoon, all three slash stones until the tone comes out *clear*.
Honestly, that's the worst gym class ever.
Meanwhile Luna's old nanny admits they've spent *five years* investigating the attempt on Jin's life, with no leads.
Luna has a bad feeling, so she tells her to *investigate* Miu and Anne.
Next day Jin trains until he *pukes*, because his aura is nowhere near enough to make a stone ring.
Jed popped a stone without any aura at all. Jin can't do that, so he trains *harder*.
Jed watches him and he's *impressed*. He says Jin might even break Luna's record.
Then Jed sulks, because if Jin had been born ten years earlier, he'd have the whole clan in his *hands*.
A month later the intermediate class lines up for the first *missions* of the year.
Half of them will die, and their squad leader tells them to write their *wills*.
Jin's brothers get shipped off to a diplomatic ceremony as *punishment*, and they groan about it.
Jin gets something far *worse*. His mission is to assassinate a man named Alcaro Chanderer.
Alcaro is one of the many lovers of Talaris Endorma, the ruler of the Secret Palace, who shows no *mercy* to anyone who hurts them.
His brothers freak out. Mahmeet is a lawless region, and only guardian knights go there on *missions*.
Jed admits Alcaro's own family wants him dead, because they'd rather kill him than let him leak their *secrets*.
Jin says he'll do it. Jed likes the *resolute* answer, and his brothers scream that he's being sent to die.
Jin leaves in a disguise, with a hood and a different hair color, while Gilly sees him *off*.
Murakhan hisses at him to get going, and not to *boast* around.
Mahmeet is where the filthiest criminals in the world *gather*.
A thug twice his size picks a fight with the new guy. It ends fast, with *blood* on the bar.
The barkeep likes him after that, and tells him about a new *drug* going around town.
And there's an inn called the Moonlight Well, where the kings of Mahmeet *stay*.
Alcaro is there too, a spoiled count's son who's crazy about *pleasure* and has nothing but a good bloodline.
He screams at his guards because he's out of drugs, and the guards stare back *cold*.
One guard even wishes he'd die of an *overdose* already. That's loyalty for you.
Jin can't use poison, because it's forbidden in town, and he can't kill Alcaro in the *open* with those guards around.
He slams his hand against the wall and says he's *decided*.
Meanwhile a lady from the Secret Palace arrives with her men, and she's here to *kill* Alcaro too.
Jin's plan is *insane*. Mix shadow force into a four-star lightning spell, and it hits like a six-star spell.
And who would suspect a fifteen-year-old? Even the legends only reached six stars *recently*.
He steps up to the window, shadows spreading under his feet, and mutters that this is one crazy *idea*.
Lightning Call! The *sky* answers him.
The inn goes up in a six-star *blast*, and Alcaro's guards go flying.
The Secret Palace lady walks right into the *crater*, wondering who the hell attacked.
Jin survives only because of a *pendant*, and that last crack of lightning hit like a seven-star spell. Ouch.
She thinks he got caught in the attack and walks *over* to him. Her men say Alcaro is gone anyway.
Now the problem is what happens *next*, so Jin hides his face and plays along.
The local kings tell her to back off. She answers with a *sword*.
So Jin plays the coward. He was frightened, he hurt his leg, and she *buys* it.
She smiles and tells him to think of it as a fond *memory*.
Jin waves goodbye with a grin. Mission *complete*.
But the one person hunting the sorcerer just *helped* him up.
